title: Elementary charge and charges of particles
body: The elementary charge e is the magnitude of the charge of a single electron or proton and can be considered to be the smallest indivisible amount of charge; an electron has charge -e, a proton has charge +e, and a neutron has no electric charge.
ced_evidence: 8.1.A.1.ii–iii: "The charge of an electron is −e and the charge of a proton is +e, and a neutron has no electric charge."
correction_note: product-owner-directed correction by the Claude session (David, 2026-10-10): the escalated row was corrected against its own CED evidence and re-checked by both independent checkers and the own-family veto
